_about: Data for the Dungeon Flow page (Claude writes it, the page reads it with the .cs files). kids: boxes one layer down. steps: a list, top to bottom. flow: steps left to right, p = the step that calls it, fn = its function. code: [file, first line, last line] from the repo root. Unity skips Flow~ (no .meta).

root.s: What Unity calls, in the order it calls it

title.s: Type a channel, press Enter Dungeon

flow.d: The input field's button calls this. Data is a static class that is not in this repo.
The Enter button. The scene change starts Awake on every object in DungeonRoom.
Writes "You entered:" and the typed text on screen, then the scene loads.
Not at load: the first enemy death or first weapon pickup calls this, once.
Only with unifiedChat on: opens a Twitch or YouTube reader. False falls back to Lexone.
Joins the channel through the Lexone IRC package, and listens for its chat lines.
Sets irc.channel and reconnects when chat is quiet. No Lexone or WebGL: our own reader.

gm-awake.s: The singleton, cameras, the UI, frame rate

flow.d: A second GameManager removes itself. This one stays across scenes.
UI Cam is a child of the main camera.
Uses the scene's UI, or makes one from uiPrefab. That runs UI.Awake right away.
vSync off so targetFrameRate counts.
One Image per child of healthUI.
Each slot image, and its first child as the reload image.
The enemy name box and the dialogue box.
The child named "Fill" under each weapon icon.
Only when showCharge is on: the child named "Charge".
On each room's floor tilemap. DungeonRoom.bounds reads this; spawning and pathfinding stay inside it.
The room hands it on.
The static everyone plays sounds through.
Gets a kinematic body so it receives trigger events.
Runs when a weapon animation is made in an attack, not at load.
No Awake: found (or made) the first time anything reads a switch.
No Awake: loaded from Resources on first use (the fist).

start.s: Objects read each other, before their first Update

flow.d: Hands the player's max HP and HP to the UI.
Copies heart[0] until there are enough, then shows maxHP of them.
Hearts below HP get the full sprite, the rest the empty one.
Finds the SoundPlayer; UpdateMusic uses it for room music when the room changes.
HP starts at maxHP; the setter also updates the hearts.
_maxHP from the Inspector (4 by default); setting it changes the heart count.
Every HP change goes straight to the UI. No event, just a call.
Hearts below HP get the full sprite, the rest the empty one.
Takes GameManager's Controller and remembers where it stands as the respawn point.
invincibleTime is now, so isInvincible starts false.

enemy-start.s: HP, home, sprite, layer, spawn as trigger

flow.d: HP from EnemySO. born starts its 24 h life; home is where it walks back to.
The asset each enemy reads: speed, HP, stats, knockback, notice range.
Finds the sprite it tints red when hurt, and keeps its color to go back to.
It never rotates, and goes on the Enemy layer.
A trigger so it does not shove things; Update turns that off once it is free.

map-start.s: Pairs doors, finds the room you are in

flow.d: Filled in the editor (OnValidate), inactive rooms too.
Every RoomTrigger, inactive ones too, then each one gets a partner door.
Each door's partner is the nearest door in another room.
The active room holding the player becomes currentRoom.
The room's floor area, measured by its Spawner in Awake.

ui-start.s: Canvas camera, mini map, weapon icons

flow.d: Draws through the UI camera that GameManager found in Awake.
Adds the MiniMap component; it builds itself in its own Start.
Puts each hand's weapon icon in its slot.
The held weapon's uiWep sprite in each slot. Called again on every pickup or throw.
Its own Start: two panels (corner, big), a content layer for room pictures, and you.

small-start.s: Camera, chat object, dialogue, items, locks

flow.d: The Cinemachine camera follows the player.
Grabs the Lexone IRC object. It does not connect yet.
OnStart dialogue boxes call the UI right away (the first room's intro).
Its own dialogueText when sequence is None, else that named sequence.
The named sequences.
Keeps the lines and when they started; UI.Update types them out.
Gets a sprite and a trigger collider if the prefab has none.
Weapon loot shows the weapon's uiWep sprite.
Plays the item's idle animation.
Runs on the first frame of each attack. No timer and no speed: gone after two physics steps.
On a character: finds it and shows the buff's effect.
With locks off in Experimental, every lock starts open.

physics.s: FixedUpdate, then trigger events (triggers come in no fixed order)

fixed.s: Things that slide: thrown weapons, boomerangs, loot

flow.d: Slides, bounces, then lands as loot.
A circle cast ahead; walls stop or bounce it.
Keys open locks. Enemies take damage; a crate or maxHits stops it.
Only once: BecomeLoot makes it Loot after this physics step.
Spins slower as it slows, or points the way it flies.
Out until it stops, then back to the owner.
Straight at the owner through walls, speeding up; returns the distance left.
Slows down and stops.
A character it may hit, and each character only once.
An enemy of its owner's team. With no owner, any character.
Different team = enemy.
The weapon's hit sound, and its hit effect on the victim.
Made on the victim, gone when its animation ends (0.5 s without one).
The victim takes the damage, then is pushed away from the attacker.
With weapon.maxHits set, the HitBox is gone after hitting that many characters.
Only a physical attack hurts a crate; then the HitBox is gone.
Without a destroyTimer, the HitBox ends at its first touch.
The HitBox carries the weapon's BuffEffect. Its own trigger copies it onto the one hit.
Removes what the enemy resists. Not stackable: renews the old one instead.
A HitBox with a destroyTimer is removed by Update when time is up.

damage.s: What each kind of target does with damage

flow.d: Shows its name, turns red, takes damage minus defense (at least 1). At 0 HP, Update calls Died.
Hit sound. Then skipped while invincible or shielded. Otherwise HP drops and the hearts update.
True if any BuffEffect on it has one of these types.
One unlocked hit opens it: HP straight to 0.
Locked while its keyId is not empty.
A push away from the hitter, slightly random, minus resistance. Stuns until it slows down.
Pushed like any Character, weakened by its enemyData.knockbackResistance.
Skipped while invincible.
Physical hits only. Changes sprite per hit, drops loot when broken.
Paths are redone, it may be destroyed, and its loot drops.
Path grids re-read the walls from the next frame.
The Loot prefab, and/or the weapon as new Loot.

enemy-died.s: Loot, unlock for chat, then gone

flow.d: The first death anywhere connects chat. The sprite's tint is cleared.
Reads the channel typed on the title screen.
Only on the first frame it is dying.
The loot prefab, and/or a weapon as a new Loot object.
Each new loot slides away; a landing thrown weapon keeps its size instead.
A real death (not old age) unlocks this enemy for chat summons.
Only unlocked enemies can be summoned.
The first kill of a kind keeps a hidden copy without loot.
An unlocked summonable enemy with this name, or null if none yet.
Waits half a second, Died running each frame, then it disappears.
A chest does not disappear: it opens, drops its loot once, shows the open sprite.
While overlapping: off cooldown, not dying, and the other is a Character of another team.
Different team = enemy.
Knockback first, then damage (magic or physical).
Once per cooldown: the next touch waits enemyData.cooldown seconds.
Only the player picks loot up. By type: a weapon goes to a hand.
An empty (fist) hand takes it. Both full: hold the attack button of the hand to swap.
A hand with no weapon or a CQC one takes it. Pickup sound, loot gone.
Filling the left hand connects chat, to the channel typed on the title screen.
Hand and loot trade weapons; the loot shows the old one and is pushed away.
By type: a chat skill is learned.
Adds the skill to availableSkill if new, then the loot is gone.
By type: an instant item is used at once.
The player uses the item, then the loot is destroyed.
A Heal item heals now.
No heal while berserk. Capped at maxHP. The effect plays once.
After any pick, the weapon icons refresh.
Each hand's weapon sprite is shown in the UI.
The same item placed in a level, without Loot.

room-trigger.s: Leaving a door trigger switches room

flow.d: While stunned, speed toward the next room is cut, like a wall.
Only the player counts.
Only if the player walks toward the paired door.
The new room turns on, the old one off (its enemies get OnDisable). New respawn point.
The clip for the room's type.
Cached walls and paths are dropped next frame, so enemies find ways in the new room.
Summons and potions waiting are dropped in a new room.
Not ghosts (ignoreCollide), not floating characters.
True if any BuffEffect on it has that type; here, floating.
Fall clip or shrink. Others are destroyed; the player respawns at the room entry.
Back to where it entered the room.
Only the teams it heals. isHealing picks the water animation.
The heals flags must hold the character's team; Player only by default.
In its Update: 1 HP each tick to everyone inside.
Heals, then plays the heal animation (GameManager.healEffect) on it.
Berserk blocks it; HP never goes past maxHP.
Makes the effect on the character and destroys it after its animation (0.5 s if none).
Leaves: no more heals, normal animation.
Old Input axes first; the new Input System overrides them. Hides the cursor when the mouse is idle.
A gamepad sets everything and returns: keyboard and mouse are not read.
isPressedOnce gives true once per press, per name ("dialogue", "throw", "minimap").
WASD moves, arrows look, O/P attack, Q throw, M map.
-1, 0 or 1 from a pair of keys.
Off by default (Experimental.disableMouse). When on: aim at the cursor, clicks attack.
It turns on when moved far enough, off after a second still.

chat.s: Chat lines into queues and votes

flow.d: The first kill or first weapon pickup connects to the channel typed on the title screen.
Twitch or YouTube, picked from the channel text.
When unifiedChat is off: the IRC package's events.
Pings and reconnects Lexone; with no Lexone (or WebGL) it opens our own reader.
Lexone calls it for each chat message; the display name and text go to addToDB.
Its Update empties the queue the reader thread fills.
Skill votes first. Then summon to the line, teleport right away, potion to its line.
The first word (or its start) and the word count pick the type.
A skill word is a vote. Enough voters: the skill casts on the player.
Waits in summonQ. Too long (300): cleared.
Only inside the current room, onto an empty spot.
The first room whose bounds hold the spot.
Hands the chatter and potion name to ChatPotion, which picks the line.
Queued as "potion name": in the potion line, or the summon line with potionSamePool.

gm-update.s: Takes one summon or potion per cooldown

flow.d: With testWithoutChat on, a mockEnemy spawns near the player every testWithoutChatSpawnCooldown seconds.
Keys 1-6 vote for the six chat skills, for testing.
Vote like one chatter.
A potion whose turn it is goes near the player, before the summon line is read.
Also passes the summon line, where potions wait when potionSamePool is on.
From its own line or the summon line. A room gets potionsPerRoom at most.
On a free spot near the player; slides like dropped loot and counts in potionsSpawned.
Asks for the next summon every frame; spawns it unless testWithoutChat is on.
Only when the spawn skill is off cooldown. Taking one starts the cooldown.
Takes whose turn it is, then finds the enemy by its name.
The chatter with the fewest turns goes first, then the oldest.
Must be unlocked (killed once).
Sets lastUse to now, so isReady is false for cooldown seconds.
Into the current room, within spawnRangeFromPlayer of the player.
Under the room's "Enemies" object, so it turns off with the room.
Flood fill from the player in half-unit steps; a random free cell 0.5 to range away.
For now death is a reset: full HP, back to the first room.
Full HP (a test for now), back to position 0,0, then the first room.
Current room off, first room on; the summon and potion queues are cleared.
movement is clamped to 1. Experimental switches: 0 in attack clips; looking follows movement or the look input.
StuntMech lets a knockback slow down by itself; otherwise velocity is set straight from movement.
While the floating buff lasts, knockback slows down less (floating.friction, else 1).
While stunned, velocity decays and true skips walking; under 0.5 the stun ends.
While Throw is held the weapon buttons throw, and this frame has no attack.
Left hand, then right hand.
Idle, walk or the weapon type's attack clip, in the facing direction.

attack.s: From a held button to a HitBox in the world

flow.d: A charge skill can block the normal attack. Then: weapon off cooldown and button down.
ForceAttack skips the cooldown check (charge skills call it too). Uses the weapon, then animates.
Starts the cooldown, plays the weapon's own animation and sound, then makes the hitbox.
The weapon's anim object plays its clip for the player's facing.
Placed in front of the player, then filled from the weapon: damage, knockback, buff, flying speed.
An extra shift set in the weapon for each direction: up, right, down, left.
Weapon damage x the user's attack stat x berserk.
Speed 0 stays where it spawns; else its Rigidbody2D flies along flyDir.
The AI/ hook after each hitbox: keys, Multi hits, boomerangs.
Sets the state UpdateAnim reads: the weapon type's attack clip, timed to the cooldown.

charge.s: Hold a weapon button, let go for the skill

flow.d: The press itself attacks. Holding blocks repeats. Letting go fires the skill if it charged.
The player sprite turns half yellow while a hand is charged.
True once getChargePercent reaches 1. Blocks asks on release, Glow for both hands.
0 to 1 over chargeTime, 1 = charged. The UI can read the same number.
Multi runs as its own coroutine. Others start the cooldown, play sound and anim, set the attack clip.
Normal attacks, cooldown plus interval apart. Its hits may skip knockback or stun (OnAttack).
Big, Spin and Volley spawn at once; Flurry and Lunge are coroutines over the next frames.
Back into the same SpawnHitBox the normal attack uses.
count hits along dir, 0.08 s apart; the later ones resume after Update on later frames.
Dashes along dir, frozen so it can't walk, then one hit after 0.15 s.

throw.s: Hold Throw, press a weapon button

flow.d: Held: tries both hands, and blocks attacks this frame.
Not the fist, not on cooldown, once per press. The hand becomes a fist.
A new object with a sprite, collider and slide body.
An empty hand.
Both weapon icons show their hand's uiWep sprite again.
Each physics step it slides and spins; when it stops, it lands.
Keys open locks. Enemies take damage; crates stop it.
If the key fits the Lock on other, it unlocks; usedUp means the key is gone.
An enemy of the thrower, once each: sound, effect, damage, knockback, buff. Non-magic hits damage crates.
Only once: done ends the flying and touching, then BecomeLoot starts.
After the physics step, it becomes a Loot weapon.
The weapon as a new Loot (sprite, trigger) in the room; OnDrop keeps its thrown size.

anim.s: Picks the clip from state and facing

flow.d: An attack clip plays to 90% before anything else.
The facing follows looking, to pick the clip.
Up, right, down or left from looking. stopFacing keeps it a moment.
Sideways when x passes 0.71, else up or down.
Idle, walk (water versions when healing), or the weapon type's attack clip.
Plays the facing clip unless already playing. Attack clips speed up to fit the weapon cooldown.
Back to idle or walking; an attack sets state again through ForceAnim.
A child object played in the facing clip; it removes itself at 90%.
Removes itself at 90%.

enemy-update.s: Notice the player, find the way, walk

flow.d: Spawned as a trigger. Once it touches nothing it turns solid (ghosts stay triggers).
Red tint ends. Dies after 24 h or at 0 HP.
The first death anywhere connects chat.
Reads the channel typed on the title screen.
Only the first frame it is dying.
The Loot prefab, and/or the weapon as new Loot.
A real death (not old age) unlocks it for summons.
Chat can summon only unlocked enemies.
The first kill of a kind keeps a hidden copy, no loot.
Died runs each frame until then.
Opens once, drops its loot, shows the open sprite. Never destroyed.
Knocked back: skip walking this frame.
Velocity decays; under 0.5 the stun ends.
Flips the sprite. Notices within noticeRange.
To the player if noticed, else home.
A grid per body size, BFS from the target.
Pushed away from close enemies.
Up, right, down or left for the animation.
Unless stopFacing holds it.
Sideways past x 0.71, else up or down.
When no Enemy is left (chests count), it fires its UnityEvent once and removes itself.
Searches again only once the last found enemy is gone or off; new summons count.
Cached walls are dropped next frame, so enemies walk through the opened doors.

True once the sword Loot is gone: picked up or fallen in a hole.
Cached walls are dropped next frame, so enemies walk through the opened doors.
Set in the Inspector. Opens, stops blocking, hides after its animation.
Waits as long as its longest clip, then hides the door.
OnCall dialogues are called the same way.
Stores the lines for UpdateDialogue; a press already held won't skip the first line.

ui-update.s: Fills, chat text, dialogue, mini map

flow.d: Each hand's reload shows on its weapon icon.
0 to 1 since the last use.
Only with showCharge: the weapon icons need a Charge image, like Fill.
0 to 1 while a charge skill's button is held; 0 when not charging.
Every frame, so the slots fill up as the cooldowns run.
Slot 1 summon, slot 2 potion cooldown.
0 to 1 since the last use, like a weapon's.
Only if the UI has a chatText box.
Who cast what, and open votes.
Every frame; with no text left the box is hidden.
Freezes the player. Typewriter text; left attack skips or goes on.
Stunned for 1 s, renewed each frame the dialogue shows, so no walking.
True the first time each name asks, until the button is let go.
Shown 2 s when an enemy is hit.
Shows the name box, waits 2 seconds, then hides it.
Its own Update: rooms, doors, you. M opens the big map: player off, paused if bigMapPauses.

coroutines.s: Resume after Update when their wait is over

flow.d: Waits for the fall clip, then removes or respawns.
Back to where it entered the room.
One frame after the room turns on: moves it along the path it could have walked.
A grid per body size, BFS from the target.
Shows the enemy name box, hides it after 2 s.
Hits spaced in time: one HitBox every 0.08 s.
Normal attacks in a row, a gap apart; stops if the weapon changed.
Dash, then hit.
Rise, hold, land.
Random pushes on all.
After its animation.
Ends when time is up or the character died.
Slow, stun, stop facing, stop animation each frame. Burn and heal once a second.
Flags, so one buff can be several.
Stunned for the next second; called each frame while the buff lasts.
Keeps its facing 0.1 s; called each frame while the buff lasts.
Each kind of target takes the damage its own way.
HP up, at most maxHP; nothing while berserk.
Checked by Player (shields), Heal (berserk), Hole (floating).
Below the weapon, closer as it slows.

onoff.s: Rooms switch on and off, things end

flow.d: Remembers when.
By Experimental switches: walk home, heal, forget you, clear buffs.
A frame later: moves it as far along the path home as it could walk.
HP up, at most maxHP; nothing while berserk.
For now: full HP, back to 0,0.
Current room off, first room on: their enemies get OnDisable / OnEnable.
Empties the summon and potion queues for the new room.
Animator plays again; the effect goes.
The hand is ready again.
Closes the socket.
Unpauses if the big map was open, frees the room pictures and camera.
